A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLC research, with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, concept-recognition fine-tuning and scaling experiments, and ViperGPT analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds backbone, distribution-shift, driving-task, corruption, symbolic-program, rule-extraction, and runtime experiments in Appendices F–I.

M1.justification: The main VLM-recognition-plus-SDD pipeline remains unchanged. Appendix G.2 adds a tested MNLogic variant that executes recognized digits through a Python XOR program instead of an SDD. The rule-extraction study is exploratory, rather than an established replacement for VLC's supplied-rule assumption.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained three tasks and object-count shifts, v2 evaluates digit recoloring and rotation, previously unseen KandLogic colors and shapes, and the SDD-OIA driving task with four action outputs. Appendix H also adds natural-language-to-symbolic-rule generation as an evaluated task.

E2.justification: The external comparator set remains End2end RS/FT, Prism, and ViperGPT; the GPT-4o versus CodeLlama comparison was already present. Appendix G.2 newly compares SDD-based VLC with a Python-rule implementation. Extending existing baselines to additional datasets does not itself change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Original experimental settings are retained. New protocols include InternVL3.5-8B-Instruct with greedy decoding, appearance perturbations, SDD-OIA action-configuration splits and four-label exact-match accuracy, controlled concept corruption, and rule extraction using five descriptions per task with compilation-validity and truth-table-alignment metrics. Appendix I adds wall-clock inference measurement.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial robustness and diagnostic analyses: backbone transfer, appearance shifts, controlled perception-error propagation, circuit-versus-code substitution, symbolic-rule acquisition failures, and inference efficiency. These test generalization, error sources, symbolic-module necessity, and practical limitations beyond v1's retained fine-tuning, scaling, and ViperGPT analyses.

E5.justification: The retained experiments still use five seeds, numbered 0–4, with means and standard deviations. New stochastic studies follow the same five-repetition convention. No revised run counts, uncertainty estimators, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and earlier plotted results are unchanged, while Tables 3–6 and Figures 15–17 add extensive outcomes. For example, Figure 15 reports SDD-OIA OOD accuracy of 43.32% for fine-tuned VLC versus 15.00% for End2end FT. New Table 4 inconsistently repeats fine-tuned MNAdd-3dgt accuracy as 84.46%, versus 86.46% in Table 2; this is not an established performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds an explicit accuracy-bound argument: entirely correct concept vectors yield correct outputs under exact rule execution, so task accuracy is lower-bounded by exact-match concept accuracy. The original Boolean task definitions and equations remain unchanged, with no substantial new theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain intact. v2 explicitly restricts robustness claims to supplied deductive rules and controlled shifts, while the abstract changes 'strong performance' to comparative OOD superiority. That superiority wording is broader than Table 1 supports: ViperGPT scores 91.18% versus VLC's 89.97% on KandLogic-5obj.

C2.justification: Interpretation expands substantially: v2 discusses task- and shift-dependent fine-tuning generalization, code substitution for circuits, difficulties in automatic rule acquisition, and flexibility-versus-runtime tradeoffs. It also explicitly excludes conclusions about open-ended multimodal robustness. Earlier limitations concerning supplied rules, task-specific modules, and recognition errors remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and newly discloses Hugging Face decoding settings: do_sample=True, temperature=1e-6, and repetition_penalty=1.05. It also supplies the alternative Python program and inference timings. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, and prompts remain; the decoding disclosure does not establish a change to earlier experiments.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. The Yang et al. discussion of natural-language rule translation is relocated and reused in Appendix H, rather than introducing a new reference.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained. v2 makes local wording and terminology refinements, adds scope qualifications and appendix cross-references, updates publication text, and appends Sections F–I. The expansion primarily documents new studies rather than extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables and three numbered figures covering the new evidence. Existing figure images are retained, but captions are extensively revised, Figure 4 changes from a two-by-two arrangement to one row, Table 2 and other displays move, and publication headers and colored links alter the presentation.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone, appearance-shift, and driving-task evaluations substantially address v1's narrow empirical coverage. Circuit-versus-code, corruption, and rule-acquisition studies clarify the source and boundaries of robustness, while scope qualifications and decoding disclosures improve interpretation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the localized Table 4 versus Table 2 numerical inconsistency and the abstract's overly broad superiority wording.
